question: Please explain what is "Human intelligence"
answers: Human intelligence is the intellectual capability of humans, marked by complex cognitive feats and high levels of motivation and self-awareness. Through intelligence, humans possess the cognitive abilities to learn, form concepts, understand, apply logic and reason, recognize patterns, plan, innovate, solve problems, make decisions, retain information, and use language to communicate. There are conflicting ideas about how intelligence is measured — whether it's fixed at birth, or malleable depending on an individual's mindset and efforts.

I think it’s our ability to figure things out, learn from what’s happened, and adjust. It’s not just being good at facts. It’s also reading people, handling new situations, and knowing when you don’t know something.

question: Should you co-sign a personal loan for a friend or family member? Why or why not?
answers: What it amounts down to is that this is a personal choice. You cannot receive reliable information as to whether co-signing is a good move due to lack of information about the specific person and situation. You know if they are reliable, if they will be able to pay off the loan without the banks needing to come after you. This is wholly a personal decision for the person involved, and them alone to make based on the facts that they know and others don't.

There are many different responses to this but i think that it depends a lot on the relationship and how well you actually know their financial situation. Co-signing means you're on the hook if they can't pay, the bank doesn't care about the friendship, they just want their money, and it comes out of your credit either way. I think it's only worth doing if you'd genuinely be okay paying the whole thing yourself if it went wrong, because emotionally that's basically what you're agreeing to. If saying no would wreck the relationship anyway, that's worth being honest with yourself about too.

I'd lean toward no unless I could genuinely afford to lose that money without it affecting my own life. Co-signing means the debt is legally yours too, and it's easy to underestimate how much that can strain a relationship if things go wrong. If I really wanted to help, I'd rather just give what I could afford outright instead of tying my own credit to someone else's ability to pay.

question: What caused World War 2?
answers: The main causes of World War II were nationalistic issues, unresolved issues, and resentments resulting from World War I and the interwar period in Europe, in addition to the effects of the Great Depression in the 1930s. The culmination of events generally understood to have led to war were the 1939 invasion of Poland by Germany and Soviet Russia and the 1937 invasion of the Republic of China by the Empire of Japan.

It was really a mix of things that built up over time — the harsh terms placed on Germany after WW1 left a lot of resentment, and the economic collapse of the Great Depression made things worse across Europe, which let extremist movements gain real power. Aggressive expansion by Germany, Italy, and Japan, combined with other countries' reluctance to intervene early, eventually made war unavoidable.

World War II was caused by unresolved tensions from World War I, the rise of aggressive totalitarian regimes, economic instability, and a failure of international diplomacy to stop territorial expansion

question: Please explain what is a "Strategic game"
answers: A strategy game is a game in which the players' uncoerced, and often autonomous, decision-making skills have a high significance in determining the outcome. Almost all strategy games require internal decision tree-style thinking, and typically very high situational awareness. Strategy games are seen as a descendant of war games, though war is not the whole story of what defines the genre.

A strategic game is a game that requires you to fully think about your every move, critically. It's not a game that is based on luck or pure instinct, but it's a game that is structured in a way that compels players to have a plan and a strategy in order to win.

question: Describe a moment when you felt truly proud of yourself. What led up to it, and why did it matter to you?
answers: I went through a breakup during exam season and spent a lot of that time crying, honestly not believing I'd pass. Studying felt impossible, but I still pushed myself to do my best in every exam. When my results came back, I was so proud — I got 67% in Media and 75% in Criminology, and passed everything else too. It mattered because I didn't think I had it in me to pull through, and I did.

I felt truly proud when I received university recognition for academic excellence, after being stuck in a course I didn't enjoy. It meant so much because it felt like confirmation that I was on the right path. It might seem like a small achievement to others, but it felt like a giant leap for me.

For me it was receiving academic recognition , I got awards for term 1 this year. I wrote my exams while I was sick and could barely study properly, but I still passed and made it into the grade 11 top ten, ranking 8th in the whole grade and 4th in my class. It mattered most because it proved I'm capable of more than I'd ever achieved without giving it my all.

Finishing my first big project after weeks of doubting I could. I almost quit twice, but I kept going one small piece at a time. When it finally worked, it mattered because it showed me I could follow through on something hard.

question: Think of a time you felt completely misunderstood by someone close to you. What happened, and how did you handle it?
answers: In high school, I had a group of friends who used to gossip about another friend of mine, who was also part of the group. I always spoke up against it and defended her, because I don't like it when people gossip about someone they call a friend. When she found out they'd been gossiping about her, not from me,they blamed me anyway, since I was always the one calling them out. She then assumed I must have gossiped too, and asked why I hadn't told her if I hadn't. I felt attacked and completely misunderstood. I didn't really do anything about it — I just let it be until they eventually realised I was innocent and only wanted peace. That's usually what I do when I'm misunderstood: I let people believe what they want to believe.

I once felt misunderstood when someone thought that i was asking question to investigate a certain situation when really i was just really concerned about them and i handled the situation by being silent because i understand that silence is a virtue in such situations and left them to think whatever they wanted to think about me.

A close friend assumed I was ignoring them when I was actually just burned out and overwhelmed. Because they read my distance as coldness, I took a step back to collect my thoughts, then reached out directly to explain how exhausted I’d been. Clearing the air brought us much closer.

question: How would you describe home? Is it a place, a feeling, a person?
answers: Home is a feeling. In matric, I didn't feel at home in my own house because I isolated myself so much while studying — I'd leave at 6am and only get back at 7pm every day. I felt at home at my friend's place; it was fun and warm and I spent most of my time there. I also felt at home last year at the res I stayed at, because of the people and how our landlords treated us like family, braais, movie nights, it felt like a family gathering. I also feel at home when I'm with my friends. It's the warmth, the laughter, and feeling comfortable enough to just be yourself.

Home, to me, is both a place and a feeling. It's the one place you can go where you won't feel judged, pressured, or frowned upon under any circumstances. It's a place of comfort, peace, and love — somewhere that once your feet touch the ground, you feel whole and complete.
I would say that home is everything above. It could be a home and it could be a feeling, whatever place that makes you feel comfortable is what I would consider a home

Home is less about a specific address and more about where I can be fully myself without performing for anyone. It's usually tied to people rather than a place — wherever my closest friends or family are, that's where I feel settled. I've lived in a few different spots, but only some of them ever actually felt like home, and it was always because of who was there, not what the place looked like.

Home isn't tied to one address for me — it's more about which spaces let me switch off and just exist without effort. I've felt at home in places I only lived in for a few months, purely because of who was around. So I'd say it's mostly a feeling, but one that almost always traces back to people rather than the walls themselves.
Home is where you can exist without performing, where you feel understood without explaining yourself, and where you can simply be.

Home is more than a place; it’s a feeling of belonging. It’s where you can exist without pretending, where silence feels comfortable, and where you’re accepted even in your most imperfect moments. Sometimes, home is a person, a memory, or a version of yourself you’re learning to embrace.

question: If you could redesign one everyday object to make it better, what would you change and why?
answers: I'd redesign the bed by adding a built-in warmer ,a system that lets you set your preferred temperature before sleeping, so the bed is already warm when you get in. It would basically eliminate the need for blankets.

I'd redesign umbrellas so they could actually handle wind without turning inside out. Something with a more flexible frame that bends with a gust instead of snapping against it, and maybe a quick-release panel that pops open under pressure and reseals itself once the wind dies down. It's such a basic object that still fails at its one job the moment weather gets bad.

question: Complete the sentence: "The thing I wish more people understood about me is... because..."
answers: I have a very big heart, and people think I move on too quickly because I like dating around, but really I'm just afraid of being alone with myself and my thoughts, with no one to share them with. Being alone with your own thoughts can be scary.

The thing I wish more people understood about me is that I'm still figuring life out , I'm not perfect. I've made a lot of mistakes, hurt people, and lost friends along the way. The pressure to be seen as a 'good example' has cost me some genuinely once-in-a-lifetime experiences. I want people to understand this because it would take a lot of weight off my shoulders.

The thing I wish more people understood about me is that I process things slowly before I react, because I'd rather think something through properly than say the first thing that comes to mind and regret it. People sometimes read that as me being distant or not caring, when really I just need a bit of space to figure out how I actually feel.

I wish that people understood that when I am quiet, they have truly outdone themselves and that I have really run out of things to say and have run out of all hope for them. Silence from me is not a good sign, at all.
